name: Toolkit
description: Central host for external MCP servers and API connectors — connector instances expose invocable tools and background broadcasts (with optional durable queues).

endpoints.name: listMcpServers
endpoints.description: Lists the workspace's registered external MCP servers.

endpoints.name: createMcpServer
endpoints.description: Registers an external MCP server (http/sse). Name must be unique in the workspace.

endpoints.name: updateMcpServer
endpoints.description: Updates name/url/transport/headers/enabled/scope. Only provided fields change.

endpoints.name: deleteMcpServer
endpoints.description: Removes an MCP server.

endpoints.name: importMcpServers
endpoints.description: Bulk-imports the standard `{ "mcpServers": { … } }` JSON (VS Code / Claude Desktop / Cursor). stdio entries are skipped.

endpoints.name: listConnectorTemplates
endpoints.description: The connector template gallery (fields to render config forms, commands, broadcasts).

endpoints.name: listConnectorInstances
endpoints.description: Connector instances of the workspace (all templates).

endpoints.name: createConnectorInstance
endpoints.description: Configures a new instance of a connector template. Config values for secret fields are encrypted at rest. Runs healthCheck before saving; a failing check is a 502 unless force=true.

endpoints.name: getConnectorInstance
endpoints.description: One instance with its tools (commands) — the instance page's payload.

endpoints.name: updateConnectorInstance
endpoints.description: Updates name/config/enabled/scope. Secret fields left masked in the request keep their stored value. Re-runs healthCheck on config changes.

endpoints.name: deleteConnectorInstance
endpoints.description: Deletes an instance with its queues and state.

endpoints.name: checkInstanceHealth
endpoints.description: Runs the template's healthCheck against the stored config and records the outcome.

endpoints.name: runInstancePoll
endpoints.description: Runs one background poll immediately (emits broadcasts for any detected changes).

endpoints.name: listTools
endpoints.description: Every available tool across enabled instances (optionally ?templateId= filters). Tool names are `<instance>_<command>` (slugified instance name — stable, id-free). Trusted app callers (e.g. Artisan) pass ?agentId= (+ x-twodb-space-ids via the gateway) to get only tools that agent may use; without it, the full workspace list returns.

endpoints.name: invokeTool
endpoints.description: Invokes a connector tool and returns `{ output }`. toolId is either the id form `<instanceId>.<command>` (webapp) or the agent-facing NAME `<instance>_<command>` — name-form calls should carry ?agentId= (Artisan sends it) so access lists are enforced. Required/number params validated by toolkit.

endpoints.name: listAgents
endpoints.description: Proxies Artisan's agent list (id, name, type, description) for the workspace — the catalog the access picker builds from. 502 when Artisan is unreachable.

endpoints.name: listBroadcasts
endpoints.description: Recent broadcast events (newest first). ?instanceId=, ?event=, ?since= (ISO ts), ?limit=.

endpoints.name: streamBroadcasts
endpoints.description: Server-sent events of broadcasts as they are emitted (one SSE `data:` line per event). Same filters as /events for the initial snapshot behavior — stream emits only new events.

endpoints.name: listQueues
endpoints.description: Queues of the workspace (optionally ?instanceId=) with pending counts.

endpoints.name: createQueue
endpoints.description: Requests a named durable queue for an instance's broadcasts — every emitted event is also inserted, so nothing is lost when a live broadcast is dropped. Idempotent per (instance, name).

endpoints.name: deleteQueue
endpoints.description: Deletes a queue and its undelivered items.

endpoints.name: nextQueueItem
endpoints.description: Claims the oldest pending item (marks it delivered). 204-style empty result when the queue is drained — { item: null }.

endpoints.name: peekQueue
endpoints.description: Looks at up to ?limit= items (default 20) without claiming them.
